title: Self-Dual Endo-Classes
body_html:
Self-Dual Endo-Classes

Let $F/F_0$ be an extension of degree at most $2$, with Galois group generated by $x\mapsto\overline x$.

A based extension $(E,\beta)$ of $F$ is self-dual over $F/F_0$ if the involution on $F$ extends to an involution on $E$ which sends

$$ \beta\longmapsto -\beta. $$

If $\beta\ne 0$, then $E/E_0$ is quadratic, where $E_0$ is the fixed field of the involution.

The draft uses an involution

$$ \sigma:\mathscr E(F)\to\mathscr E(F) $$

on endo-classes. If an endo-class $\mathfrak c$ contains a ps-character supported on $\beta$, then $\sigma(\mathfrak c)$ contains a ps-character supported on $-\beta$. The involution preserves degree and fixes the trivial endo-class.

An endo-class $\mathfrak c$ is self-dual if

$$ \sigma(\mathfrak c)=\mathfrak c. $$

In this case the draft states that $\mathfrak c$ contains a ps-character supported on a self-dual element.

Conflict Note

The older spec/endo/def/self-dual-extension.md says "a self-dual element $\beta$ satisfies $\beta=-\beta$". That is not the formulation used in the current TeX. The current TeX says the involution sends $\beta$ to $-\beta$.
